desc:
Return every binary string of length n in which no two 1 characters are next to each other. Each string is returned as a row of n integers, each 0 or 1.

For n = 3 the answer has 5 rows: [0,0,0], [0,0,1], [0,1,0], [1,0,0] and [1,0,1]. Rows may be returned in any order.
hints: Build a row one position at a time. At each position you choose 0 or 1.
Writing a 0 is always safe. Writing a 1 is safe only if the previous value is not a 1.
Pass the previous value (or a flag) down the recursion and only ever extend rows that are already valid, so that nothing needs to be filtered at the end.
editorial: Use depth-first search over positions. At position i you may always place a 0; you may place a 1 only when the last placed value is 0 (or when i = 0). Because every partial row is valid by construction, each complete row of length n is a valid answer and is produced exactly once.

The number of answers follows the Fibonacci numbers (2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... for n = 1, 2, 3, ...), so the search does work proportional to the output size. Generating all 2<sup>n</sup> rows and filtering would also pass for n ≤ 10 but wastes effort on rows that are doomed early.
time: O(n * F(n)) where F(n) is about 1.62<sup>n</sup>
solution:
def noAdjacentOnes(n):
    res = []
    row = []

    def go(prev):
        if len(row) == n:
            res.append(row[:])
            return
        row.append(0)
        go(0)
        row.pop()
        if prev == 0:
            row.append(1)
            go(1)
            row.pop()

    go(0)
    return res
